about: Conservation lighting limits by medium: the museum's only lux-by-medium numbers. Art maps each work's medium to one class and sends Light an FLightTarget (lux range, colour temperature, UV, annual dose). Art.WithinCare checks every reference moment and the annual dose. A work of mixed media takes the class of its most sensitive component.

reproductions.what: A true-size reproduction made for display in the original's place and credited to it: a pigment print on cotton rag for a print or a stereograph, a duplicate transparency for an autochrome. The original stays with its holder.
reproductions.credit: Exhibition facsimile after the original in
reproductions.note: Museums show facsimiles where the light would harm the original (the Hall of Light's daylight, D-014). The facsimile keeps its original's care class, so its record says what the original needs; its own fading is not conserved but answered by replacing it, from its measured dose. Care therefore accepts it under any light.

evidence.row: Facsimiles may also be used to avoid overexposure of the original artifact.

surrogate facsimile copies of original documents and photographs for exhibition: important when the original might be damaged through too much handling or is too light sensitive to be placed on display

doseAccounting.note: Annual exposure is illuminance on the work times the hours it is lit in a year. The museum never closes (D-006), so presence-linked gallery light, not opening hours, bounds the hours; the annual limit, not the hour count, is what Art.WithinCare holds.

evidence.row: each day of exposure is assumed to be 8 hours, each year 3,000 hours

sourceSpectrum.note: The catalogue's LED luminaires emit almost nothing in the UV and IR; the UV limit still binds daylight through glazing, which is filtered (D-014).

evidence.row: a light spectrum without IR and UV radiation
the spectrum of the LED includes almost no radiation in the infrared and ultraviolet ranges
